text:
alex: Quick Q — traveling to London next month for client meetings. Can I book flights on my personal card and get reimbursed? Also what's Redwood's per-diem for international trips?

maya_people_ops: Short answer: yes, you can use a personal card if you don't have a corporate card available, but prefer booking via the Redwood Travel Portal when possible. For reimbursements: submit the report in Expensify within 14 days and attach original receipts.

maya_people_ops: Per-diem: we use a simplified per-diem for international travel — $120/day USD for meals & incidentals (covers breakfast/lunch/dinner + small incidentals). You can either claim per-diem or submit actual meal receipts, not both.

priya: Do we need pre-approval for business-class or premium seats? My flight to LHR is 9.5h.

maya_people_ops: Good point — economy is default. Premium economy/business is allowed for single-leg flight >8 hours but requires manager + People Ops approval in advance. If it's >12 hours we will also consider. Always add approval screenshot or approval note to the Expensify report.

andrew: If I lose a taxi receipt, what's the process?

maya_people_ops: If you lose a receipt, submit a Lost Receipt Form in Expensify and include a short note + manager sign-off. For small amounts (<$25) we can accept a credit card statement line plus a note from you and your manager.

alex: For hotels — must we use the vendor on the travel portal? I'm seeing a cheaper option on a different booking site.

maya_people_ops: Use the Travel Portal rate when available (preferred vendors give negotiated rates + insurance). If you find a materially cheaper option outside the portal, book it but flag in the expense report and include a 1-2 sentence justification; manager will approve/deny. If the hotel has an invoice that can be billed to Redwood directly, that avoids reimbursement delays.

priya: Any special rules for per-diem on travel/training days? For example, travel day into country vs full days?

maya_people_ops: Per-diem rules: first and last calendar day are prorated. On travel days we payout 75% of the daily rate by default; full days = 100%. If you submit actual receipts, we follow actuals instead of per-diem.

andrew: Timeline — how long for reimbursement once submitted?

maya_people_ops: Typical turnaround: 7–10 business days after manager approval and finance review. If missing receipts/approvals, it will be delayed. Expensify shows status updates.

alex: Example of expense note I'm adding to the report:
```
Trip: London client meetings
Dates: 2026-04-12 to 2026-04-15
Booking: personal card (economy) — receipt attached
Meals: claiming per-diem $120/day
Other: taxi receipts attached
Manager approval: Priya
```

priya: One more — foreign currency. Do we attach the merchant receipt in local currency? How does conversion work?

maya_people_ops: Attach merchant receipts (local currency). Expensify will capture the foreign amount and convert at the daily rate automatically; finance reconciles using the bank/card exchange rate for corporate cards. For personal card reimbursements we reimburse in USD at the rate used in the report conversion.

jess_expensebot: Expensify: report "LON client — Alex" created by alex — status: needs manager approval. :rocket:

alex: Thanks! I'll submit and tag Priya for approval. :thumbsup:

priya: Approved from my side once the report has receipts and the per-diem selection is clear. :+1:
